30 September 2026 Our Ref: CDD/CIF/13 
 
By Email  
 
 
To:  Chief Executives of all Authorized Insurers, Responsible Officers of all Licensed 
Insurance Agencies and Licensed Insurance Broker Companies  
 
 
Dear Sir/Madam,  
 
 
"Conduct in Focus" – September 2026  
 
The Insurance Authority (“IA”) is pleased to  publish the latest edition of “Conduct in Focus” 
today.  The publication is now available on the IA's website at the following link:  
 
https://www.ia.org.hk/en/legislative_framework/files/Conduct_in_Focus_Issue_13_EN.pdf  
 
In this edition, attention is drawn to a number of conduct matters observed in the market:  
 
Responsible practice in marketing: 
While attention-grabbing statistics may be mathematically correct at a particular point in time, 
the selective presentation of such figures in isolation without balanced context  can create 
misleading customer expectations and  may result in  breaches of applicable regulatory 
requirements. Insurers are reminded to  embed robust governance controls  and customer-
focused review process into their marketing practices, with disclosures that are fair, balanced 
and transparent, so as to  to support informed decision -making and foster long-term customer 
trust. 
 
Lessons from fake news: 
Following a recent false rumour circulating in the market concerning the alleged use of falsified 
documents to misclassify customers as professional investors, the importance of accuracy, 
integrity and effective controls in the know-your-client process has once again been brought 
into sharp focus . Insurers and intermediaries are reminded that professional investor 
exemptions are a regulatory privilege that should only be applied where customers genuinely 
qualify and where fair treatment can continue to  be demonstrated. Any a ttempts to misuse 
regulatory exemptions or  to circumvent policyholder protections would attract serious 
regulatory consequences and undermine trust in the market. 
 
Growing sophistication of KPIM: 
Drawing on insights from the IA’s latest KPIM training and handbook, this edition underscores 
the increasingly  sophisticated role of Key Persons in Control Functions for Intermediary 
Management (KPIM) in promoting ethical conduct across insurers’ intermediary channels. In 
particular, the importance  is highlighted of embedding a strong customer -centric culture, 

2 
 
designing controls that achieve their intended conduct objectives, and strengthening 
accountability throughout the agency management hierarchy.  
 
Non-compliance of self-referral arrangement: 
Attempts to disguise prohibited commission rebating and other non -compliant practices 
through so -called “self -referral arrangements”  will not withstand scrutiny. Reinforcing the 
principle of substance over form, the referral arrangements must not be used to circumvent 
regulatory requirements, incentivise unlicensed activities or undermine fair customer treatment. 
Arrangements that, in substance, operate as unchecked rebates will attract regulatory scrutiny 
and enforcement action, regardless of how they are described or labelled. 
 
Responsible Officer application assessment and interviews: 
IA assesses whether Responsible Officer applicants are fit and proper to oversee the 
compliance and governance responsibilities of insurance agencies and insurance broker 
companies. The importance of applicant’s regulatory knowledge  and practical compliance 
capabilities, particularly when the applicant is to assume a management role in a company with 
a higher conduct risk business models, drives the IA to arrange applicant interviews that will 
form part of the approval process.  This edition therefore helps explain the types of applicants 
who may be invited to such interviews and how the interviews may be conducted. 
 
Enforcement reviews underscoring the importance of agent manager accountability: 
The two recent enforcement cases discussed highlight the important role agent managers play 
in promoting ethical conduct and maintaining compliance standards. Agent managers who 
encourage, facilitate or conceal misconduct by their downlines may call their own fitness and 
properness into question and face disciplinary action. The IA reinforces its expectation that 
agent managers act as effective supervisors, uphold integrity and foster a culture of fair 
customer treatment throughout their teams. 
 
Other topics covered include the latest complaints statistics for the first half of 2026 and the 
ongoing efforts to combat fraud. 
 
Thank you for your interest and i f you have any questions or comments, please e -mail to 
conductsupervision@ia.org.hk.  
 
 
Yours faithfully,  
 
 
 
 
Alan Wu 
Head of Conduct Supervision (Acting) 
Insurance Authority  
 
c.c.  The Hong Kong Federation of Insurers  
The Hong Kong Confederation of Insurance Brokers  
Professional Insurance Brokers Association
